title: BOS-836 chat picker — the advertised [r]ename action opens an inline prompt that writes the new title through to the chat list

scenes.title: the chat picker advertises [r]ename beside the action it sits next to

waitFor.label: the session board is populated, so the picker below is opened on real fixture state and not an empty shell

steps.caption: The demo session board lists the session whose chats this scenario renames.
Open the session's chat picker — the list that owns the per-chat actions.

waitFor.label: a real chat row rendered, so the action bar below belongs to a populated picker rather than a loading frame

steps.caption: The chat picker lists the session's chats, cursor on the newest.

expect.label: the selected chat still carries its fixture title — the before state the rename is measured against
BOS-836: rename is advertised in the action bar, so the key is discoverable rather than hidden
the pre-existing per-chat actions are intact — [r]ename was added beside them, not in place of them

steps.caption: BOS-836: the action bar now offers [r]ename next to the chat actions that were already there.

scenes.title: pressing r opens an inline prompt, prefilled and editable, in place of the action bar

steps.caption: Press the advertised [r]ename key on the selected chat.

waitFor.label: the inline prompt took over the footer, so the keystrokes below are going into the editor and not the list

steps.caption: The rename prompt replaces the action bar, prefilled with the chat's current title.
Clear the prefilled title — the prompt is a real text editor, not a fixed label.
Type the new title into the prompt.

waitFor.label: the typed characters are echoed live in the prompt, so the input is focused and receiving keys

steps.caption: The typed title renders live in the prompt.

expect.label: the prompt is still open and labelled while the title is being edited
the prompt advertises how to commit the edit
the prompt advertises how to abandon the edit — the escape hatch scene 4 exercises

steps.caption: BOS-836: while the prompt owns the keyboard it advertises both of its exits.

scenes.title: enter commits the rename and the row settles under its new title

waitFor.label: the action bar is back, so the prompt closed and the list has the keyboard again

steps.caption: The prompt closes and the chat list takes the keyboard back.

expect.label: BOS-836: the renamed row carries the new title in the table, and survives the picker's next poll because the daemon accepted the write
the action bar is fully restored, rename included — the prompt was transient, not a mode the list gets stuck in

steps.caption: BOS-836: the new title is settled in the chat table with the action bar restored.

scenes.title: esc abandons a second edit and leaves the committed title untouched

steps.caption: Open the rename prompt again on the renamed chat.

waitFor.label: the prompt reopened, so the escape below is cancelling a genuinely open edit

steps.caption: The prompt reopens, prefilled with the title just committed.

waitFor.label: the action bar returned, so escape closed the prompt instead of leaving the view

steps.caption: Escape closes the prompt and returns to the chat list — it does not leave the picker.

expect.label: BOS-836: the cancelled edit left the committed title exactly as it was
the list is interactive again — escape cancelled the edit rather than backing out of the chat picker

steps.caption: BOS-836: cancelling changes nothing and hands the list back intact.
